semantic_findings.title: Project-Controlled Execution During Configuration Loading
semantic_findings.description: Configuration resolution executes project-local Python with exec_module, even for status queries without an explicit folder. Activation also runs customization hooks without an explicit trust check. An untrusted checkout can therefore execute code or supply operational instructions under the agent's permissions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The call chain directly executes a module selected from the project and instructs the agent to run configurable hooks. Exploitation requires attacker-controlled project content; no malicious hook or module payload was found in this package.

semantic_findings.title: Plan Updates Can Follow Symlinks Outside the Ticket Tree
semantic_findings.description: The loader accepts symlinked Markdown plans, and mark opens existing plans for writing without checking their resolved destination. A crafted tree can redirect an approved status update into an external writable file with matching plan frontmatter.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path.read_text and the existing-plan wb open follow symlinks, and neither path has a containment or no-follow check. Exploitation requires a crafted symlink and a readable, writable target that parses as the ticket's plan.

content.user_title: Plan and Manage Tickets with BMad
content.value_statement: Disconnected planning and status updates leave teams with unclear tickets and missing dependencies. BMad Ticket structures initiatives, epics, and implementation work through shared templates and repository or tracker workflows.
actual_capabilities: Draft initiatives, epics, stories, spikes, and bugs with requirements, boundaries, references, and verification checks.
Split epics into ordered implementation entries with explicit prerequisites and unresolved questions.
Create Markdown ticket files from planned entries and update repository ticket status in separate plan files.
Find tickets by reference or title and report readiness, dependency cycles, missing prerequisites, and entry drift.
Guide publication and synchronization through repository files, GitHub, Jira, Linear, Notion, and Trello configurations.
Estimate stories and epics using configurable scales when estimation is enabled.
limitations: The standard workflow requires BMad project setup, uv, and Python 3.11 or later.
Remote workflows require configured CLI or MCP access; available operations depend on the provider and tool version.
It prepares implementation work but does not build the requested software or independently resolve missing product decisions.
Project scripts, hooks, and ticket paths require trust; the supplied workflow does not sandbox them.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a bug ticket
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a bug ticket for [problem]. Ask for missing reproduction steps and expected behavior. Show the draft before saving or publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a planned story
prompt_templates.prompt: Find ticket [reference] in [initiative]. Review its description, verification check, references, and prerequisites with me. Preserve its identity and do not publish yet.

prompt_templates.title: Break down an epic
prompt_templates.prompt: Split [epic] into implementation entries using [requirement source]. Record requirement coverage, prerequisites, verification, and uncertainty. Validate the proposed set before requesting approval.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile and prepare publication
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [initiative] against [configured tracker]. Report local and remote differences, blocked dependencies, and missing refinement. Propose publication scope and wait for approval before remote changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate repository and tracker state

faq.question: What work does BMad Ticket organize?
faq.answer: It organizes initiatives, epics, stories, spikes, and bugs in a structured ticket tree.

faq.question: What setup does it need?
faq.answer: The standard workflow uses a configured BMad project, uv, and Python 3.11 or later. Remote stores also need authenticated tools.

faq.question: Which ticket stores are supported?
faq.answer: It ships configurations for repository files, GitHub, Jira, Linear, Notion, and Trello. Remote features depend on available CLI or MCP tools.

faq.question: Does it require a remote tracker?
faq.answer: No. The repository store manages Markdown and TOML files locally. Publication commits approved files but does not push them.

faq.question: Does it implement the planned software?
faq.answer: No. It prepares tickets for implementation and tracks their state. Building the software is a separate workflow.

faq.question: Is it safe to run in an unfamiliar repository?
faq.answer: Review project scripts, hooks, and symlinks first. Configuration loading can execute project code, and existing plan writes can follow symlinks.
